Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood. Procurement asked me to send over our suggested redlines so legal can see how fees and the implementation timeline align across Exhibits A/B. We have two asks: (1) split the implementation fee across three milestone exhibits instead of a single up-front line item, and (2) adjust the throughput pricing ramp to reflect pilot months.

I attached our redlines (Mediflow_redlines_v1.docx). Can your team confirm whether Redwood is able to accept a phased SOW with milestone sign-offs? If so, we also need an outline of the DocuSign path and a suggested change order template so our legal ops can queue it.

Appreciate it,

Hi Alex — thanks for sending the redlines and context. 

Short answer: yes, we can do a phased/split-fee approach. High-level plan from our side:
- Redwood will produce a single addendum (change order) that amends Exhibits A/B to split the implementation fee into three milestone payments tied to acceptance gates.
- Throughput pricing will include a pilot floor for months 1–3 and a ramp to the committed tier thereafter.
- Our Legal will run a short redline pass and provide a counter; CS will draft an implementation sequencing attachment (milestones + acceptance criteria).

I'm looping in Monica (legal) and Markus (CS) to review Mediflow_redlines_v1 and confirm the redlineable items + any risks. Monica — can you confirm whether any standard MSA language prevents milestone invoicing? Markus — can you draft a short implementation_timeline.xlsx we can attach to the change order?

Proposed next steps:
1) Internal redline pass (2 business days)
2) Redwood counter to Mediflow with tracked changes and proposed Milestone Exhibit (DocuSign-ready)
3) 1-week legal ops turnaround on their side

I will hold a short sync if folks prefer to talk through the acceptance criteria; otherwise I can send the counter and attach the timeline.

—Ben

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Mediflow redlines — legal notes and proposed edits

Ben / Markus — quick legal pass below after reviewing Alex's doc: Mediflow_redlines_v1.docx. I flagged three areas that need careful language and suggested alternatives in track:
1) Fee reallocation: ok to split into three milestone invoices, but we should preserve a partial non-refundable mobilization fee (10%) to cover reserved capacity and onboarding.
2) Acceptance gates: tighten acceptance criteria language to avoid broad 'successful integration' phrasing; reference test plan and sample prompt set acceptance (attach to Exhibit).
3) Ramp pricing: propose a firm pilot floor and clear trigger for when committed throughput pricing applies (e.g., sustained usage over 30-day window).

I attached Redwood_counter_redlines.docx with tracked comments and a redline of the MSA clauses we touch. I also added suggested language for an "Implementation Attachment" that lists milestones, deliverables, and acceptance artifacts.

Risks: if Mediflow insists on full refundability of mobilization fee we may need approval for a short credit holdback to cover unused reserved nodes. Also, procurement may push for invoice net-60; our standard is net-30 unless there's a procurement-approved exception.

I'll mark the counter as DocuSign-ready once we finalize the milestone table. Markus — if you can share the timeline spreadsheet today, I'll merge it into the attachment.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_counter_redlines.docx (docx, 42KB)

Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 11:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Mediflow redlines — legal notes and proposed edits

Adding the implementation_timeline.xlsx (attached). High-level milestones:
- Milestone 1 (Pilot kickoff): SOW sign + mobilization (2 weeks) — deliverable: staging cluster + runbook
- Milestone 2 (Pilot acceptance): Pilot performance tests + prompt set validation (4 weeks) — deliverable: acceptance signoff doc
- Milestone 3 (Production cutover): Production rollout + baseline monitoring (2 weeks) — deliverable: go-live checklist

I've included billing triggers next to each milestone (invoice due on milestone acceptance; sample GL codes). Net-30 remains standard; we can propose Net-45 for enterprise accounts but need Sales leadership approval.

Let me know if Monica wants any additional acceptance artifacts in the spreadsheet.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: implementation_timeline.xlsx (xlsx, 18KB)

Subject: Re: Request: synchronize fee exhibits + SOW edits for phased rollout

Alex — thanks for your patience. Attached is Redwood's counter (Redwood_counter_redlines.docx) and an implementation timeline spreadsheet (implementation_timeline.xlsx) that maps milestones to invoices and acceptance artifacts. Summary of key changes: 
- Implementation fee split: 10% mobilization (non-refundable), 45% Pilot acceptance, 45% Production cutover.
- Pilot pricing floor: fixed throughput floor for months 1–3; committed pricing applies after 30 consecutive days above the floor.
- Acceptance: acceptance criteria now reference the attached test plan and sample prompt set; a signed acceptance form constitutes milestone acceptance.
- Billing: default Net-30; if Mediflow requests Net-45, we'll escalate to Sales Ops for approval.

Next steps from our side: please review the counter and timeline; if OK, we'll prepare a DocuSign change order and send for signature. If you prefer a quick 30-min legal sync to review tracked changes, I'm happy to set one up early next week.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
